question.problem:
Consider the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x-{60}^{∘})-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=0$ for $-{90}^{∘}\le x<{90}^{∘}.$ If the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ are written in **ascending order**, what are their values?

${x}_{1}=${{field-1}}${}^{∘},\,$
${x}_{2}=${{field-2}}${}^{∘},\,$
${x}_{3}=${{field-3}}${}^{∘},\,$
${x}_{4}=${{field-4}}${}^{∘}$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

First, we rearrange the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x-{60}^{∘})-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} & =0 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(4x-{60}^{∘}) & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-{60}^{∘} & ={60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}, & \, & \, & 4x-{60}^{∘} & ={120}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & ={120}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} & \, & \, & 4x & ={180}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} \\ x & ={30}^{∘}+n\cdot {90}^{∘} & \, & \, & x & ={45}^{∘}+n\cdot {90}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $-{90}^{∘}\le x<{90}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x={30}^{∘}$ and $x={45}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=-1$ gives $x=-{60}^{∘}$ and $x=-{45}^{∘}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $-{90}^{∘}\le x<{90}^{∘}.$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=-{60}^{∘},-{45}^{∘},{30}^{∘},{45}^{∘}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
x={-60}^{∘},\,{x}_{2}={-45}^{∘},\,{x}_{3}={30}^{∘},\,{x}_{4}={45}^{∘}
$$
